findings.finding: The limitation inputs Hearings 1-3 already found missing remain missing, confirmed by an independent re-read of facts.json and procedure/limitation.md this session: the EDT is still ASSUMED (F-002), the ACAS EC certificate date ('Day B') is still ASSUMED (F-003), and the ACAS EC contact date ('Day A') is still UNKNOWN (F-004). procedure/limitation.md's own calculation remains an admitted illustrative proxy (92 calendar days standing in for 'three months', run through scripts/deadline_calculator.py on the assumed EDT) rather than a real calendar-month figure from a documented date. This is not a new finding - it is the fourth consecutive hearing on which it is unmet - but this hearing's own remit (deadlines actually verified, not recalled) requires it to be checked again rather than assumed cured, and it is not cured.

A more basic procedural gap than the date-verification gap above, not named as a discrete finding by Hearings 1-3: nothing in facts.json, final/case_theory_memo.md, or opposition/opposition_case.md states that an ET1 has actually been presented, or on what date. issues.json's own evidence_missing list for ISS-001 already flags 'the actual date the ET1 was, or will be, presented - not stated anywhere in the facts supplied', but no prior hearing's disposition addressed this squarely as a procedural-compliance finding in its own right. procedure/limitation.md's conclusion that 'today's date still falls inside the primary period' answers whether a claim would presently be in time if presented - it does not, and cannot, confirm any claim has actually been instituted. This hearing's own remit is procedural compliance, and confirming that the proceeding this workflow is testing has actually been commenced is a threshold procedural fact this record does not supply.

The repeated, unexplained non-production of two specific, named, allegedly-existing primary documents (the termination letter/HR record fixing the EDT, and the ACAS EC certificate itself) has now gone unmet across all four hearings held to date, with no explanation offered anywhere in the record at any point. Hearing 3 directed that if this persisted to Hearing 4, this hearing should 'treat this as having crossed from a disclosure gap into a case-management failure a real tribunal would very likely have already acted on, not repeat this as a fourth routine request.' Applying that direction: this Tribunal's own assessment is that a real Employment Tribunal, exercising its Rule 29 (further-particulars/unless-order) and Rule 37 (strike-out) case-management powers on this exact fact pattern - a precondition set at Hearing 1, repeated at Hearings 2 and 3, and now unmet a fourth time with total silence as to why - would very likely already have made an unless order, and a continued failure to comply with one would expose the relevant heads to strike-out independent of their substantive merits. This Tribunal does not itself make such an order (this workflow does not model that interim procedural layer, and this hearing tests merits-and-procedure-readiness, not case management in the first person), but it records this plainly rather than issuing a fourth routine repetition of the same request, exactly as directed.

The Further and Better Particulars of the protected disclosure(s) for ISS-003/ISS-004 - content, recipient, form, date, public-interest belief basis, and sequencing against the disciplinary process - remain completely unmet for a fourth consecutive hearing. F-010 and F-012 are both still UNKNOWN on independent re-read this session. This sits inside, not alongside, the case-management finding immediately above: this is the single most concrete example of the pattern that finding describes, because it is a request for information a genuine claimant bringing this claim would already hold (the content of their own disclosure, to whom they made it, and when), not a document that must be obtained from a third party or awaited from disclosure.

The asymmetry Hearing 3 first found - the claimant's case theory declines to engage ERA 1996 s.43B(1) as amended by ERRA 2013 s.17 and the Chesterton Global v Nurmohamed public-interest test at all (final/case_theory_memo.md Section 7, on the stated ground that Chesterton is unlogged in authorities.json), while the opposition's case now does exactly that engagement (opposition_case.md Part B.1(i), independently verified this round via four convergent secondary sources) - remains unaddressed one hearing later, confirmed on this session's own re-read of both documents in full. Declining to cite an unlogged authority is a defensible interim position on citation discipline; declining to engage the underlying statutory test itself, which does not depend on any authority being logged to exist, is a different thing and remains an open gap in the claimant's own theory for the lead heads.

Hearing 2's authority-logging repair (Burchell, Iceland Frozen Foods, Polkey, Chesterton Global v Nurmohamed, J v DLA Piper, and the ERRA 2013 s.17 amendment, to be logged in authorities.json with schema-conformant, verification-tracked entries) remains unmet, confirmed by independent re-read of authorities.json this session: it still runs only to AUTH-007, and none of the six sits in it. This is now the third consecutive hearing this exact repair has gone unmade. It bears directly on this hearing's own remedy analysis: Polkey v A E Dayton Services Ltd is the doctrinal basis for the ISS-009 compensatory-award-reduction mechanism this hearing must assess, and for the purposes of this matter's own record it remains not yet part of the verified authority base, notwithstanding the opposition's own credible convergent-secondary-source verification narrative for it in prose.

Remedy availability in principle, assessed for the first time at this hearing rather than merely asserted: for ISS-003 (s.103A), reinstatement or re-engagement (ERA 1996 ss.113-117) and, failing either, a basic award (s.119, calculated by age, a week's pay subject to the statutory cap, and complete years of service) plus a compensatory award are available; general legal knowledge (not independently verified against legislation.gov.uk this session, consistent with this role's Read/Grep/Glob-only tool contract) holds that ERA 1996 s.124(1A) disapplies the ordinary statutory cap on the compensatory award specifically for s.103A dismissals, but this is flagged UNVERIFIED rather than relied on as settled. For ISS-004 (s.47B), compensation under ERA 1996 s.49 is understood on the same general-knowledge basis to sit outside an analogous cap; whether injury-to-feelings compensation is additionally available for a detriment (as distinct from a dismissal) claim has no authority presently logged in authorities.json for that specific proposition, and consistent with how every other unlogged authority has been treated throughout this matter's record, this Tribunal declines to rely on it as established.

F-008 (continuity of employment) has a materially different legal effect at this remedy-and-procedure stage than at the liability stage already tested at Hearings 1-3: it does not gate ISS-003 or ISS-004 at all (neither carries a qualifying-period requirement), but it directly controls the quantum of the basic award component of remedy under ERA 1996 s.119 for either head if liability is ever established, since that award is calculated by complete years of service. F-008 remains UNKNOWN, so even a claimant who fully proves ISS-003 or ISS-004 at Hearing 5 could not presently have the basic-award component of remedy quantified - only the (potentially uncapped) compensatory-award component could be assessed in principle. ISS-002, correctly run only as a contingent secondary head, remains gated outright by the same unresolved fact and would in any event carry a materially weaker, capped remedy if the gate is eventually cleared.

ISS-009's remedy-adjustment mechanisms (Polkey deduction; TULRCA 1992 s.207A ACAS Code uplift of up to 25%) remain correctly described as available in principle, unchanged from Hearing 2's doctrinal settlement of that point, but cannot be given any percentage or qualitative value on the present record. A Polkey assessment requires comparing what the disciplinary process actually was against what a fair one would have looked like; an uplift assessment requires knowing whether the ACAS Code was followed. Hearing 3 already found the disciplinary file and the stated reason for dismissal (F-020) entirely absent from the record, and nothing in the case theory, the opposition case, or facts.json has changed that position since. This hearing's own remedy-availability test therefore answers 'available in principle, unassessable in practice' - the necessary, unchanged consequence of Hearing 3's evidence finding, not a fresh discovery.

A pleading-and-framing point genuinely proper to this hearing's remedy-and-procedure remit, not previously raised in these terms: opposition_case.md Part B.1(iii) identifies that if the contradictory internal emails (F-013), once produced, prove to be an individual co-worker's unauthorised act rather than a management decision, ERA 1996 s.47B(1A) (inserted by ERRA 2013 s.19, already independently verified live against legislation.gov.uk in this matter's own record at AUTH-002) gives the claimant a direct cause of action against that individual as an additional respondent, with the employer separately and vicariously liable subject to its own 'all reasonable steps' defence. Whether that possibility should actually shape how this claim is framed - who should be named as a respondent - cannot presently be assessed, because both the authorship of F-013/F-014 and the correct identity of the primary Respondent itself (F-025) remain unknown. This is named because a genuine procedural-compliance and remedy hearing should flag a live joinder question the record cannot yet answer, not because it can be resolved today.

The disability-discrimination cluster (ISS-005 to ISS-007) and victimisation (ISS-008), struck at Hearing 1 for want of an identified impairment, PCP, or protected act, are not revisited. Neither final/case_theory_memo.md nor opposition_case.md attempts to reintroduce them with new content; both correctly treat Hearing 1's strike as settled.

The claimant's case theory memo repeats an internal-repository observation (also previously noted, and correctly declined, at the now-superseded prior hearing-4.json on disk) that agents/solicitors/ROLE.md's declared tool contract (Read, Grep, Glob, WebSearch, WebFetch) cannot itself execute scripts/deadline_calculator.py, which its own 'Procedure' sub-function requires. This Tribunal - simulating an Employment Tribunal deciding M1-KESTREL on the merits and procedure actually before it - has no jurisdiction over this repository's own role-file consistency and does not rule on it. What this Tribunal can and does confirm, within its own remit of checking that deadlines were actually verified and not recalled, is that procedure/limitation.md's own calculation was in fact produced by invoking that deterministic script rather than by recollection - the methodological requirement this hearing exists to test was followed - even though the date inputs fed into it remain unverified assumptions, which is a separate deficiency already addressed above.

Confirm and correctly name the Respondent (F-025) - directed at Hearings 1, 2 and 3, unmet for a fourth consecutive hearing, and now also directly relevant to whether a co-worker should be joined as an additional respondent under ERA 1996 s.47B(1A) once the authorship of F-013/F-014 is known.

Build an actual Evidence Ledger and obtain the disciplinary process file, the stated reason for dismissal (F-020), and the authorship/content of the contradictory internal emails (F-013/F-014) - directed at Hearing 3, still not done. Independently verify ERA 1996 s.124(1A)'s disapplication of the compensatory-award cap for s.103A dismissals, and whether injury-to-feelings compensation is available for an ERA 1996 s.49 detriment (as opposed to dismissal) claim, against legislation.gov.uk or a properly corroborated secondary source, before either proposition is relied on in a real pleading or at Hearing 5. Both are stated in this hearing from recalled general legal knowledge only and neither is presently logged in authorities.json.

Whoever runs Hearing 5 should read this record - a genuinely re-run Hearing 4, not the version of matters/M1-KESTREL/moot/hearing-4.json this record supersedes - and should not treat the previously filed hearing-5.json as settled prior record. It rests on a 'Hearing 2' and case-theory/opposition documents that, per Hearings 1-3's own findings, did not exist in the form it purports to test, and should be rerun against the real Hearings 1-4 records and the real final/case_theory_memo.md and opposition/opposition_case.md that now actually exist.
disposition:
Hearing 4 (PROCEDURE_AND_REMEDY), M1-KESTREL, England & Wales Employment Tribunal. This Tribunal reads and builds on the real Hearing 1 (JUSTICIABILITY_AND_PLEADABILITY), Hearing 2 (DOCTRINAL_AND_AUTHORITY_CHALLENGE), and Hearing 3 (EVIDENCE_AND_PROOF) records supplied to it, and on the real final/case_theory_memo.md and opposition/opposition_case.md that now actually exist in the workspace. This record supersedes the version of matters/M1-KESTREL/moot/hearing-4.json previously on disk in full: that version, however internally coherent, rests on the same broken evidentiary chain Hearing 1 already identified - it purports to build on a 'Hearing 2' and case-theory/opposition documents that either did not exist, or did not exist in the form it describes, at the time it was produced - and is not treated as settled prior record for that reason, independent of whether its conclusions happen to converge with this hearing's own.

No issue is struck or newly cleared at this hearing; that is not this hearing's function. ISS-001 (limitation) remains undecided, on the same footing as Hearings 1-3: the EDT and ACAS Day A remain assumed and unknown respectively, and this hearing additionally finds, for the first time, that no fact anywhere in this record confirms an ET1 has actually been presented or on what date - a more basic gap than the date-verification gap already found, and squarely a procedural-compliance finding proper to this hearing. ISS-002 remains gated by unresolved continuity of employment (F-008); ISS-003 and ISS-004 remain the correct lead heads in principle but rest on Further and Better Particulars of the disclosure(s) that remain completely unproduced for a fourth consecutive hearing; ISS-009 remains a parasitic remedy issue whose doctrine is sound but whose Polkey/uplift adjustment cannot be given any value on this record; ISS-005 to ISS-008 remain struck and are not revisited.

On remedy: reinstatement/re-engagement and, in principle, an uncapped compensatory award for ISS-003 (subject to independent verification of ERA 1996 s.124(1A), not carried out this session), uncapped s.49 compensation for ISS-004, and a capped award for ISS-002 if and only if continuity is eventually proved, are all legally available in principle. Polkey deduction and the ACAS Code uplift under TULRCA 1992 s.207A remain doctrinally available for ISS-009 but wholly unassessable in practice, because the disciplinary file and the stated reason for dismissal this mechanism depends on have never been produced - the direct, unchanged consequence of Hearing 3's evidence finding. This matter is accordingly not ready for a remedy determination, for the same underlying reason Hearing 3 found it not ready for a liability determination: the evidence both depend on has still never been produced.

On procedure: this hearing goes further than Hearings 1-3 were asked to on the pattern of non-production itself. Two specific, named, allegedly-existing primary documents (the termination letter and the ACAS EC certificate) and the disclosure particulars for ISS-003/ISS-004 have now gone unproduced across four consecutive hearings, with no explanation offered anywhere in the record at any point. Consistent with Hearing 3's own direction to this hearing, this Tribunal's assessment is that a real Employment Tribunal would very likely already have exercised its case-management powers - an unless order at minimum - on this exact pattern, and that continued silence into Hearing 5 would leave the relevant heads genuinely exposed to strike-out on procedural grounds, independent of whatever the underlying merits eventually turn out to be. This Tribunal does not itself make such an order; it names the exposure plainly, as directed, rather than issuing a fifth identical request when Hearing 5 comes.

Costs are not assessed at this hearing, consistent with the workflow's own sequencing.
reasons:
I read workflows/five-hearing-adversarial.md, agents/judiciary/ROLE.md, schemas/hearing.schema.json, and every file in matters/M1-KESTREL/ - facts.json, issues.json, authorities.json (confirmed it still runs only to AUTH-007), chronology.json, chronology_gaps.md, procedure/limitation.md, research/research_log.md, intake/matter.json, scripts/deadline_calculator.py (read, not executed, consistent with this role's declared Read/Grep/Glob-only tool contract), and the real Hearing 1, Hearing 2, and Hearing 3 records supplied to me, cross-checked against the files actually on disk at matters/M1-KESTREL/moot/hearing-1.json, hearing-2.json, and hearing-3.json (confirmed these are the genuine, re-run records - substantively identical in every conclusion to what I was given, differently worded in places, consistent with having been independently authored rather than copied - and not the stale versions Hearing 1 found unreliable). I also read the version of matters/M1-KESTREL/moot/hearing-4.json that was on disk before this record was written, precisely so I could check, rather than simply assume, whether it rested on the same broken evidentiary chain Hearing 1 identified for the old hearing-3/4/5.json files. It did: it opens by citing 'Hearings 1, 2 and 3' in a form consistent with the real records, but nothing in this matter's own record establishes that the real Hearing 2 or the real case-theory/opposition documents existed at the time it was produced, and Hearing 1's own finding was that hearing-4.json specifically rested in part on a 'Hearing 2' that was never filed. I therefore did not treat its findings as prior authority for anything, even where my own independent reading happened to reach substantially the same conclusions on remedy availability and on the procedural-compliance pattern - that convergence is my own reading of the actual, now-complete record speaking a second time, not deference to a document Hearing 1 already found unreliable.

I did not re-decide any point Hearings 1-3 already resolved. I did not revisit the ISS-005 to ISS-008 strike, the doctrinal soundness of Kuzel/Beatt/Fecitt-as-corrected, or whether liability can presently be proved (Hearing 3's own remit, already answered). Instead I applied this hearing's own assigned task - procedural compliance actually verified rather than recalled, remedy availability, and relevant discretion - to the record as it stands today, and checked compliance with every outstanding repair from Hearings 1-3 against the documents that actually exist, independently re-reading facts.json, authorities.json, procedure/limitation.md, final/case_theory_memo.md, and opposition/opposition_case.md in full rather than trusting any prior hearing's characterisation of their current content.

On procedural compliance specifically, I applied Hearing 3's own explicit direction to this hearing verbatim: having confirmed the disclosure-particulars gap (F-010/F-012) and the EDT/ACAS-certificate gap remain unmet a fourth time with no explanation anywhere in the record, I named the case-management exposure plainly - a real tribunal likely already entitled to an unless order, with strike-out a live risk if Hearing 5 repeats the same silence - rather than issuing a fourth routine repetition of the underlying request, exactly as I was directed to do. I stayed within this hearing's own boundary in doing so: I have not purported to make an actual unless order or strike-out order myself, consistent with the workflow's own 'before hearing 1' section stating this workflow tests merits-and-procedure readiness rather than simulating the interim case-management layer itself.

I found the ET1-presentation-date gap independently by re-reading facts.json end to end and cross-checking it against issues.json's own evidence_missing list for ISS-001, rather than assuming the limitation analysis in procedure/limitation.md was complete because it was thorough on the dates it did address - a calculation of whether a claim would be in time if presented is not the same finding as confirmation that one has been. This is a genuinely new procedural-compliance finding proper to this hearing's own remit, not a repetition of Hearings 1-3's date-verification finding.

On remedy, I worked through what is actually available for each surviving head by independently applying the statutory scheme (ERA 1996 ss.113-119, 124(1A), 49; TULRCA 1992 s.207A) to the issues actually pleaded, rather than adopting either case document's characterisation uncritically, and flagged every proposition not independently re-verified against a primary source this session as UNVERIFIED, consistent with this matter's own verification-labelling convention and my Read/Grep/Glob-only tool contract. I distinguished F-008's differential effect on liability (gates ISS-002 only) from its effect on remedy (controls the basic-award quantum for ISS-003/004 even though it does not gate them) by reasoning directly from the statutory basic-award formula in ERA 1996 s.119, not by adopting any prior characterisation of the point. I confirmed, by re-reading Hearing 3's own findings and this session's own facts.json, that nothing has changed to make the Polkey/uplift assessment for ISS-009 possible - the disciplinary file and stated reason for dismissal remain as absent now as they were at Hearing 3 - and said so rather than performing an assessment on the illustrative or assumed facts the record has been careful, throughout, to flag as merely illustrative.

I added no new entry to authorities.json myself, consistent with Hearings 1-3's own practice - that ledger is maintained by the solicitors/opposition roles, not by this Tribunal - and declined to rule on the recurring internal-repository tooling observation about agents/solicitors/ROLE.md's tool contract, for the same jurisdictional reason Hearings 2-3 gave for similar out-of-scope observations. I did independently confirm, within my own remit, that procedure/limitation.md's calculation was actually produced by invoking scripts/deadline_calculator.py rather than by recollection, which is the specific methodological requirement this hearing exists to test, separate from and not curing the deficiency that its inputs remain unverified assumptions.
concessions_made: Neither final/case_theory_memo.md nor opposition/opposition_case.md attempted to revive ISS-005 to ISS-008, correctly treating Hearing 1's strike as settled.

The doctrinal basis for ISS-009's Polkey deduction and ACAS Code uplift, as settled at Hearing 2, remains correctly described; the deficiency this hearing finds is entirely that neither mechanism can be quantified on the present record, not that the underlying doctrine is wrong.

Today's date still falls inside the primary three-month limitation period even on the claimant's own worst-case assumed arithmetic, as both procedure/limitation.md and opposition_case.md Part A.1 correctly and consistently note - the live limitation problem remains proof that presentation was, or will be, in time (and, this hearing adds, proof that presentation has actually occurred at all), not a present finding that the claim is out of time.

The opposition's own account of the co-worker 'all reasonable steps' defence and of Gallop's risk to the Respondent's own knowledge defence remains candid and genuinely two-edged, not overstated in the Respondent's favour, consistent with Hearings 2 and 3's assessment of the same document.

The six new authorities the opposition relies on continue to be treated as available doctrine to test on their merits once logged - none is doubted as fabricated - the deficiency is that they remain unlogged in this matter's own authority ledger, not that they are suspect.

hot_bench_questions.question: Four hearings in, why does this Tribunal still not have the ACAS EC certificate or the termination letter - two documents both sides agree exist?
hot_bench_questions.answer_summary: Not answerable from the record. No explanation for the non-production appears anywhere in facts.json, final/case_theory_memo.md, opposition/opposition_case.md, or any prior hearing record, now across four consecutive hearings.

hot_bench_questions.question: Has an ET1 actually been presented in this matter, and if so, on what date?
hot_bench_questions.answer_summary: Not stated anywhere in facts.json or either case document. issues.json's own evidence_missing list for ISS-001 already names this gap; no hearing to date has obtained an answer to it.

hot_bench_questions.question: If ISS-003 succeeded outright today, what percentage Polkey reduction or ACAS Code uplift would this Tribunal actually apply?
hot_bench_questions.answer_summary: None can be given. The disciplinary process file and the stated reason for dismissal (F-020), which both mechanisms require, have never been produced at any of the four hearings held to date.

hot_bench_questions.question: If the contradictory internal emails turn out to be a named co-worker's unauthorised act rather than a management decision, should that person be joined as a second respondent - and has anyone actually asked the claimant who sent them?
hot_bench_questions.answer_summary: Cannot be answered. The authorship and content of F-013/F-014, and the correct identity of the primary Respondent itself (F-025), both remain unknown.

residual_uncertainty: This hearing's remedy findings describe what is available in principle and what cannot presently be assessed; they are not a prediction of quantum or of how a Polkey/uplift percentage would eventually land once real evidence exists - disclosure of the disciplinary file could move that question in either direction, toward a claimant-favourable finding (a plainly deficient process) or toward a low or nil adjustment (a genuinely fair process that would have produced the same outcome regardless), and nothing here anticipates which. The procedural-compliance finding that a real tribunal would likely already be entitled to case-manage this default is this Tribunal's own assessment of what a real tribunal could do on this pattern, not an order actually made within this workflow's modeled scope, and not a prediction of Hearing 5's substantive merits disposition if the missing documents do eventually surface. ISS-001 remains the same live, unresolved gate it was at Hearings 1-3, now carrying both the case-management exposure this hearing has named and a newly identified gap (whether an ET1 has even been presented) that Hearing 5 will need to address if it remains unanswered.
